# Tidewater passenger services guide

This guide describes the services Tidewater offers passengers at the
terminals and on board. Terminal staff use it to answer questions at the
ticket desk, and the booking app links to it from its help page.

## Accessibility and assistance

All three terminals have step-free access from the car park to the waiting
room, accessible toilets, and hearing loops at the ticket desk. On board,
MV Kestrel has a lift between the vehicle deck and the passenger deck and
two wheelchair spaces in the forward lounge; MV Osprey has no lift, but its
single passenger deck is level with the boarding ramp at every terminal.

Passengers who need help boarding can ask for assistance when they book or
by calling the Harlow terminal. Terminal staff meet the passenger at the
entrance, help with luggage, and board them before the other passengers.
Assistance dogs are always welcome on both vessels and in every terminal.

At Harlow, wheelchair assistance must be requested at least 36 hours before
departure, because the Harlow berth is tidal and staff need to plan which
gangway to use. Passengers who need wheelchair assistance board through
Gangway B at Harlow, which has the shallowest slope at low water; at Pellin
Island and Dunmere, where the berths are floating pontoons, assistance can
be requested up to 2 hours before departure.

## Medical equipment

Passengers may bring the medical equipment they need for the crossing.
Mobility scooters that fit through a standard door can travel on the
passenger deck of MV Kestrel; larger scooters travel on the vehicle deck
and the passenger is helped to the lift. Insulin pens, inhalers and other
personal medicines need no declaration.

Portable oxygen concentrators may be used throughout the crossing. Medical
oxygen in cylinders is also allowed, with limits: each passenger may bring
up to two cylinders, each no larger than 5 litres, and the cylinders must be
declared to Tidewater at least 24 hours before departure so that the master
can record them in the dangerous-goods list. Undeclared cylinders are held
at the terminal and returned to the passenger on arrival back at the same
terminal.

## Pets

Pets are welcome on the Pellin Island and Dunmere routes, with rules that
depend on the vessel, and pet tickets are bought in the app like any other
ticket. Pets are never allowed in the lounges or the café, and owners must
clean up after their pet.

On MV Osprey, which has no vehicle deck, a pet may travel only in a closed
carrier that stays with the owner on the open aft deck. On MV Kestrel, pets
travel in the kennel area on the vehicle deck, and owners may visit them
during the crossing only when a crew member escorts them, because the
vehicle deck is closed to passengers while the vessel is at sea. Assistance
dogs are exempt from both rules and stay with their owner.

## Lounges

Both route vessels have a main passenger saloon open to every ticket. MV
Kestrel also has the Tern Lounge, a quiet lounge on the upper deck with
reclining seats, power sockets and complimentary tea and coffee. Children
under 12 are not admitted to the Tern Lounge, and phone calls must be taken
outside it.

Access to the Tern Lounge costs £8 per person per crossing and can be added
to a booking in the app or bought on board from the café, subject to
availability. The lounge has 24 seats, so on busy summer sailings passengers
are advised to add it when they book.

## Catering

The café on MV Kestrel serves hot drinks, breakfast rolls, soup and
sandwiches on every sailing, and hot meals on the Dunmere route. MV Osprey
has a kiosk selling hot drinks and snacks. Both accept cards only. Food
from the café may be eaten in the saloon and on the open decks, but not in
the Tern Lounge, which serves only its complimentary drinks.

## Lost property

Items found on board are handed to the master and taken to the Harlow
terminal at the end of the day. Lost property is kept for 60 days and can
be collected from the Harlow ticket desk with proof of identity, or posted
to the owner for a fee. Items of value are logged in the lost-property
register and kept in the terminal safe.
